name: NVIDIA Corp
day_summary: NVDA fell -1.41% to close at $204.48 as the hawkish FOMC scenario from this morning's brief materialized: Warsh delivered a dot plot in which 9 of 18 members project rate hikes in 2026, the median fed-funds rate for year-end rose to 3.8% from 3.4%, PCE inflation forecasts were raised to 3.6% (from 2.7%), and Warsh explicitly dropped forward guidance, stating he 'can't give you any guidance on what we're going to do next.' The day's structure: NVDA opened at $209.21 in the regular session, sold through the 2:00 PM ET FOMC release and the 2:30 PM Warsh press conference, hit $203.45 on the session low, then clawed back to the $204.48 close. After-hours buying pushed NVDA back to $207.82 (+1.63% from close), essentially recovering to the prior close level — a sign that institutional buyers stepped in on the FOMC-driven flush. The one constructive read in an ugly macro day: NVDA's -1.41% made it the best-performing US mega-cap tech name — Meta fell -5.44%, Microsoft -3.79%, Amazon -3.46% — on below-average volume (126.3M vs 157.7M average), meaning sellers did not press with conviction even when macro ammunition was at maximum.

decision.rationale: HOLD at medium conviction. Critically, Warsh's explicit abandonment of forward guidance ('I can't give you any guidance') means even the hawkish dot plot isn't a commitment — the uncertainty is now structural, not event-based. Maintain stop at $195 daily close. Do not add until VIX posts a clean daily close below 17 AND the 30Y holds below 5.00%. After-hours buying to $207.82 is the strongest near-term signal — institutional capital stepped in on the FOMC dip. Thursday June 18 is the last US trading day before Juneteenth (June 19 holiday); June monthly options expire Thursday, removing the $205 max-pain gravity. Next real catalyst: August 26 NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings.

analysis:
## FOMC hawkish surprise — the scenario map plays out

The scenario map from this morning's brief resolved exactly as its hawkish branch described. Warsh delivered a dot plot where **9 of 18 Fed officials project at least one 2026 rate hike** (6 want multiple hikes), the [median rate forecast for year-end rose to 3.8% from 3.4%](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/federal-reserve-interest-rate-decision-june-17-2026), and PCE inflation projections were raised to 3.6% from 2.7%. Then Warsh did something the dot plot didn't warn you about: he [explicitly 'dropped' forward guidance](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/261974145-market-close-nasdaq-sp500-fed-inflation-kevin-warsh-spacex-tradingkey), telling reporters he 'can't give you any guidance on what we're going to do next.' That structural shift in Fed communication is the real story of June 17 — not the dot plot.

## Technical analysis

**Trend:** NVDA closed at $204.48, breaching both the 50-DMA (~$206.74) and falling further below the 200-DMA (~$213.25). The short-term trend is now bearish — this is the first close below the 50-DMA since the add-zone breakout. The long-term 200-DMA at $213.25 represents +4.2% above current price and is the level that must be reclaimed to declare the pullback over. With the 50-DMA below the 200-DMA (and widening), the death-cross risk is growing.

**Momentum:** Likely RSI in the low-to-mid 40s post-FOMC (was 45 area pre-session). Not oversold, but not recovering either. Momentum is bearish.

**Volume — the most important signal of the day:** Volume came in at **126.3M shares vs. the 157.7M daily average** — *below* average on a day when the Fed delivered its most hawkish dot plot since 2022. This is a classic positive divergence: sellers had maximum macro fuel (hawkish FOMC, raised inflation forecasts, 9/18 members wanting hikes) and still couldn't force above-average selling volume. When supply can't accelerate on the best possible bearish catalyst, the move is less trustworthy than the price action suggests.

**Pattern:** Descending from the May 14 ATH ($236.54) in a corrective phase, now testing the $200–$205 demand zone for the first time. The structure looks like a standard pullback within an intact long-term uptrend, not a trend reversal. The ATH is -13.6% away; the stop is -4.7% below current price. Risk/reward remains skewed to the bull case on any macro normalization.

**★ Strongest support — $200 round number + heavy options OI:** The $200 strike carries the highest open interest in NVDA's near-term options chain — both from retail put buyers (who are net sellers of downside risk) and institutional call writers. This OI concentration means that a $200 test draws natural demand from options dealers managing their delta. Combined with multiple prior demand-zone touches during the May 2026 recovery and the psychological significance of a round number, $200 is the real floor that would be needed to test the thesis.

**★ Strongest resistance — $206.74–$207.41 confluence zone:** The 50-DMA ($206.74) sits within 67 cents of the prior close ($207.41). NVDA closed below both today, converting both from support to resistance simultaneously. This dense zone is the level NVDA must reclaim to rebuild technical health — two tests required: first, close back above the prior close; second, reclaim the 50-DMA on above-average volume. Until that happens, rallies into $206–$207 are selling opportunities.

**Decision points:** $203.45 (session low — a second test determines whether this is the FOMC floor or a continuation lower); $205 (max pain, expires Thursday — gamma neutral above, amplified selling below); $207.41 (prior close flipped resistance).

**Invalidation:** A close above $213.25 (200-DMA) on above-average volume would invalidate the bearish read and confirm the corrective pullback is over.

## After-hours signal

NVDA recovered to **$207.82 in after-hours trading** (+1.63% from the $204.48 close), essentially back to the prior close level. This is the single most important post-FOMC signal: institutional capital is buying NVDA on the FOMC-driven dip rather than reducing exposure. The AH price is above the 50-DMA ($206.74) and above the prior close ($207.41) — if this holds into Thursday morning's open, the June expiry gamma dynamics shift from bearish (short-gamma below $205) to constructive.

## Why Warsh dropping guidance matters more than the dots

The dot plot is consensus of 18 people who disagree — 8 of 18 think rates should stay unchanged. Warsh made clear he is not bound by the median dot. His 'can't give you guidance' statement is a de facto admission that the dots are aspirational, not a rate path. For NVDA specifically: the discount-rate headwind from a potential 2026 hike is real, but Warsh's refusal to commit means the hike probability is 'possible' rather than 'committed.' The market's relatively muted reaction (S&P only -0.08%, Nasdaq +0.03%) reflects exactly this: the dots are hawkish, the chairman is agnostic. This is a Goldilocks-ish ambiguity that keeps the conditional-add gates suspended but doesn't trigger the $195 stop.
